title: Subprocessor risk-tiering and retention-discount pilot
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Validate a modular pricing addon that ties extended data retention to a standardized subprocessor risk attestation workflow, with automated SCC acceptance rules for EU/UK deals. Hypothesis: Buyers will pay a premium for 24+ month retention when the subprocessor surface is graded and minimum controls are certified; offering a retention discount tied to subprocessor risk reduces friction and increases contract conversion by >10% for high-touch enterprise opportunities.

Scope: build a pilot SKU (retention-addon-v1) enabling 13/24/36 month retention options exposed in the contract wizard and sales quote template. Implement a simple subprocessor risk-tier mapping (Low/Medium/High) driven from a spreadsheet-backed registry for pilot; discount bands: Low (0% discount), Medium (5% discount), High (10% discount) applied to retention addon price. Automate SCC acceptance flag for customers in EU/UK when all subprocessors in the selected tier have signed SCCs or are covered by our global SCC activation rule.

Acceptance criteria:
- Contract wizard shows retention options and computed price + discount based on selected subprocessor tier.
- Sales quoting template and Stripe/finance integration show discounted price and record retention term.
- Legal time to review pilot quotes reduced by 30% via automated SCC flagging.
- Measure conversion lift vs baseline (target +10% conversion for pilot cohort) and incremental ARR per closed deal.

Success metrics: conversion_delta, avg_deal_size_delta, legal_review_days, implementation_time_seconds, sales_feedback_score.

Security/Compliance: the pilot must include customer-facing subprocessor list and attestation language; cloud region residency and KMS residency options remain separate SKUs. Security review required and will run prior to public launch.

Rollout plan: 1) internal sales & SE pilot with 10 existing enterprise prospects (4 EU/UK); 2) iterate pricing bands based on buyer feedback; 3) scale to self-serve contract wizard if legal approves automation.

Trade-offs/risks:
- Keeping the risk mapping spreadsheet reduces velocity (manual updates) but avoids early integration work with the registry service.
- Discount bands may compress margin; finance must sign off on thresholds.
- Automated SCC flagging risks false positives; fallback is manual legal review which will increase SLAs for the pilot.
